hook_text: Two numbers unlock every trinomial. Here's how to hunt them in seconds.
clip_script: Before listing factors, read the signs like a detective. The product is negative — so the two numbers have opposite signs. The sum is negative — so the larger of the two, in size, carries the minus. Two conclusions before touching a single factor pair. Now the factor pairs of eighteen: one and eighteen — difference seventeen. No. Two and nine — difference seven. Yes! So the pair is negative nine and positive two. Verify both conditions: negative nine times two is negative eighteen — product correct. Negative nine plus two is negative seven — sum correct. Both keys turn; the lock opens.
visual_style: Detective-board animation: sign clues pinned up, factor pairs crossed off one by one, the winning pair circled in red string.
pacing: Quick clue-reading, rhythmic elimination of pairs, satisfying double-check finale.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and split the middle term yourself.
